e82d84cd510e127ea76cb153a175d44ad12d761f.summary: Report by Doron Karmi on the Konni malware family, a remote administration tool seen since early 2014 and potentially linked to North Korean group APT37. It describes three Konni campaigns in 2019, from January to late September, that used macro-armed Word lures, living-off-the-land tools such as certutil, a UAC bypass, and a free FTP service for command and data exfiltration. Named victims include political organizations in South Korea and Russia, plus others in Asia and the Middle East. The author notes overlap with the Syscon backdoor but cannot confirm it is the same actor.

e8bbcab2a44fbc4e9f63eab01e0c27ea3ed8215c.summary: Positive Technologies review of tools used by the (Ex)Cobalt group in 2024-2025 attacks on Linux systems. Centres on PUMAKIT, a kernel-module rootkit with a userland backdoor that hides files, processes and connections, injects an attacker SSH key into authorized_keys in memory, and captures credentials. Also covers the Octopus Rust toolkit, which carries privilege-escalation exploits and implants, and the related Facefish, Kitsune and Megatsune tools, grouped as the PUMA family.
